title: Give employees long service leave
what: Give each employee long service leave (or payment in lieu) once they reach the qualifying period of service, and keep long service leave records.

sources.title: Long Service Leave Act 1976 (ACT)
sources.locator: s 3(1) (current republication (R29, from 19 November 2025; Long Service Leave Act 1976 | Acts))
sources.quote: (1) An employee who has completed 7 years service with a single employer is entitled to long service leave for the period of the service.

sources.title: Long Service Leave Act 1976 (ACT)
sources.locator: employee records, s (2) (section number to confirm) (current republication (R29, from 19 November 2025; Long Service Leave Act 1976 | Acts))
sources.quote: (2) An employer must keep a record made under subsection (1) for an employee—

sources.title: Long Service Leave Act 1976 (ACT)
sources.locator: s 13(1) (current republication (R29, from 19 November 2025; Long Service Leave Act 1976 | Acts))
sources.quote: (1) The director-general must appoint a public servant as the registrar of long service leave.

reach.note: Every employer of employees in the ACT covered by the Act.

confidence_note: Entitlement after 7 years' service. The records section's number is to be confirmed.

assessment.summary: Employers must give long service leave after a long period of service with them. The entitlement builds up with one employer and is mostly lost on moving, which ties workers to employers; it also adds record keeping.

marks.reason: Leave builds up with one employer and is mostly lost on moving, which discourages job changes (unlike portable schemes).

assessment.confidence_note: Marked from the law's design against the framework's guide; no evaluation of state long service leave and job mobility was found.
